channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: FIFA Breach: 12.2 GB Documents Exposed
item.description: FIFA confirmed unauthorized access to personal and business data by the Handsome Boy Hacking Club. The attackers allegedly exfiltrated 12.2 GB of internal documents, including sensitive personnel records, though the group has not yet published the files. FIFA has not released a remediation plan yet; security teams should monitor for credential leaks and enforce multi-factor authentication.

item.title: Cyprus Targeted by Iranian Espionage Group
item.description: Cyprus has become a new espionage target for the Iranian threat group Volant Manticore. The group is conducting intelligence gathering against Cypriot organizations, likely collecting corporate data and credentials, though specific exploits remain undocumented. Security teams should harden network perimeter, monitor for anomalous lateral movement, and apply threat intelligence feeds on Volant Manticore activity.

item.title: 2026 Phishing Simulation Tools Ranked
item.description: The piece lists the leading phishing simulation tools for 2026, stressing the importance of click-down and report-up metrics. It notes that effective tools combine behavioral scoring, realistic spear-phishing pretexts, and a report-to-triage workflow to improve detection. Organizations should prioritize tools offering per-person risk metrics, leaderboards, and realistic content that adapts to evolving LLM-grade pretexts.

item.title: Microsoft Warns of ARTEX AI Credential Theft
item.description: Microsoft warned that state-backed hackers employ the ARTEX AI framework to locate exposed systems and steal credentials. ARTEX can transition from scanning to privileged persistence within minutes, exploiting misconfigurations and weak authentication, potentially compromising enterprise networks and cloud environments. Organizations should disable unused services, enforce MFA, and monitor for anomalous credential usage to mitigate ARTEX attacks.

item.title: 2026 Security Awareness Training Platforms Ranked
item.description: The article ranks top security awareness training platforms for 2026, focusing on engagement metrics like click-through and reporting rates. It highlights realistic simulations, per-person risk scoring, and content that avoids user fatigue to drive behavioral change. Readers should evaluate platforms offering adaptive content, robust analytics, and proven improvements in click-through and reporting.

item.title: Top Penetration Testing Firms 2026 Ranked
item.description: The 2026 penetration testing market is judged on depth of expertise, reproducible findings, and retest capabilities. The ranking highlights firms that provide actionable reports, clear remediation paths, and measurable security improvements. Security teams should evaluate these firms against engagement scope, industry experience, and post-engagement support before contracting, ensuring they maintain up-to-date testing methodologies.

item.title: Best Anti-Phishing Solutions 2026 Ranked
item.description: The 2026 anti-phishing landscape has evolved with AI-generated lures that mimic brand identities and personalize attacks. The ranking evaluates solutions on detection depth, sender verification, and the ability to block malicious links after delivery. Organizations should review the scores, test solutions against current phishing templates, and deploy the highest-rated tools to reduce credential compromise.

item.title: Mitel, Juniper, Vates, Danfoss Vulnerabilities Exploited
item.description: CISA added ten known exploited vulnerabilities, including five affecting Mitel MiCollab, to its KEV catalog. The flaws, such as CVE-2026-133275 with CVSS 5.3, enable arbitrary file uploads and other attacks, exposing sensitive data and disrupting communications across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss products. Administrators should apply vendor patches, disable vulnerable features, and monitor for anomalous activity to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: Cybersecurity Vendors Offer Black Friday 2026 Discounts
item.description: Cybersecurity vendors are offering Black Friday 2026 discounts on security tools. The promotion includes discounts on products such as Passwork, a self-hosted password manager, and other daily-use security solutions. Organizations should review the fine print, evaluate the tools' suitability, and purchase during the sale to enhance security posture while saving costs.

item.title: 4,200 Servers Exposed to AI Hacking Frameworks
item.description: Shadowserver Foundation identified over 4,200 internet-exposed servers running AI-powered hacking frameworks, up from 3,700 the day before. The report logged more than 10,000 attack events from 80 IPs between Nov 9 and 23, showing active exploitation of misconfigured AI tools.

item.title: Proxmox 9.3 Adds Production Snapshots for SAN VMs
item.description: Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.3 introduces snapshots for VMs on shared LVM storage accessed via iSCSI or Fibre Channel SANs. The update builds volume chains on thick-provisioned LVM, preserving guest identities across migrations, backups, and restores for production workloads. Administrators enable the feature via the Proxmox UI or API; no firmware or security patches are needed.

item.title: Roundcube Webmail Flaws Enable Code Execution
item.description: Roundcube released versions 1.6.22 and 1.7.7 to patch 12 flaws that could let attackers execute malicious code and expose sensitive data. The vulnerabilities stem from improper handling of attachments, message rendering, and server connections, allowing unauthorized email filter code execution and data leakage. Users should upgrade to the latest releases and verify configuration settings to prevent exploitation.

item.title: 4,400 Malicious Domains Target Holiday Shoppers
item.description: FortiGuard Labs reports over 4,400 newly registered malicious domains poised to exploit holiday shoppers. These domains, identified among 24,000 seasonal keyword registrations, facilitate retailer impersonation, payment fraud, and account takeovers, with underground markets trading stolen customer data and e-commerce infrastructure access. Security teams should block these domains, monitor for phishing, and enforce strict domain whitelisting to protect consumers.

item.title: SolarWinds Serv-U 2026.4 Patch Addresses Root Access Flaws
item.description: SolarWinds released Serv-U 2026.4, fixing 18 vulnerabilities, including nine critical flaws that could grant attackers root access on Linux servers, with lower risk on Windows. The patch also eliminates a high-severity command-injection flaw that affects only Windows installations, removing a remote code execution vector. Security teams should apply Serv-U 2026.4 immediately to close the root-access and command-injection vulnerabilities.

item.title: Google Requires MCP or CLI for Workspace AI Agents
item.description: Google announced mandatory Model Context Protocol (MCP) or command-line interface access for Workspace AI agents starting February 2027 to secure autonomous agent interactions with enterprise data. New controls include dedicated agent identities, human approval for sensitive operations, prompt injection screening, and restrictions on third-party AI tool data processing.

item.title: Survey Shows Users Will Pay to Remove Search Data
item.description: An Incogni survey of 1,008 U.S. adults revealed 55% would pay for permanent removal of personal information from public search results, while 53% desire a five-year search history log. The findings highlight growing privacy concerns over data broker exposure, with respondents valuing control over online identity footprints.

item.title: Wiz ADR Enhances Cloud AI Detection with Application Context
item.description: Wiz introduced ADR, a tool that maps runtime alerts to specific code functions in cloud environments. ADR uses agentic investigation to reduce false positives and provides precise file and line-level context for detected anomalies. Security teams can automate remediation actions directly to the affected code, improving response speed and accuracy.

item.title: Wiz Agents Celebrate Smarter Security Season
item.description: Wiz’s Red, Green, and Blue Agents highlight a quieter, smarter security season by sharing insights and achievements. The announcement showcases how the agents use data analytics to reduce noise and improve detection accuracy across cloud workloads. Users can view the agents’ performance metrics in the Wiz console, fostering a more efficient security posture.

item.title: Black Friday Amplifies Existing Consumer Cyber Risks
item.description: During Black Friday, cybercriminals intensify fraud, phishing, malware, and credential theft attacks against consumers and retailers. The surge is driven by high transaction volume, increased link clicking, and bot activity exploiting business logic and AI-driven commerce. Security teams should enforce stricter authentication, monitor bot traffic, audit business logic, and prepare AI-aware defenses to mitigate damage.

item.title: Socket CEO Discusses Vulnerability Mitigation Without Upgrades
item.description: Socket CEO Feross Aboukhadijeh appeared on the Risky Business Podcast to discuss strategies for eliminating open source vulnerabilities at scale. He emphasized that organizations can mitigate risk through runtime monitoring, automated patching, and dependency hygiene without frequent version upgrades. Listeners were encouraged to adopt continuous security practices and leverage tooling that detects vulnerable packages in real time.

item.title: Ubuntu libpcap Vulnerabilities Expose Arbitrary Code Execution
item.description: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and 24.04 LTS suffer libpcap flaws that fail to validate MAC addresses in pcap_ether_aton(), causing out-of-bounds reads and writes. CVE-2025-11961 may enable arbitrary code execution or denial of service, while CVE-2026-18238 allows malicious rpcap servers to read sensitive data or crash clients.

item.title: Palo Alto PAN-OS Targeted by Fragnesia Exploit Chain
item.description: Threat actors are chaining PHP2Shell and Fragnesia vulnerabilities to compromise Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS devices with internet-exposed management interfaces. The Fragnesia flaw enables attackers to execute arbitrary code, while PHP2Shell facilitates lateral movement, resulting in full device takeover. Administrators should update PAN-OS to the latest release, disable exposed management interfaces, and monitor for suspicious activity.

item.title: 1Password Breach: GitHub Account Compromise Exposes Customer Data and Source Code
item.description: 1Password suffered a breach when an attacker compromised an employee’s GitHub account, gaining privileged access to private repositories. The intrusion exposed customer names, emails, and internal source code, but did not reach vaults or stored passwords. 1Password responded by issuing a security advisory, rotating credentials, engaging forensic investigators, and releasing a patch to block unauthorized pushes.

item.title: Artex Tool Adopted by China, North Korea Hackers
item.description: Microsoft reports that AI tool Artex, used in high-profile breaches, is being incorporated into hacking suites by Chinese and North Korean groups. The integration expands Artex’s credential harvesting and lateral movement capabilities, potentially enabling broader compromise, though no active exploitation has been confirmed. Security teams should monitor for Artex signatures, update detection rules, and apply defensive controls against credential theft.

item.title: HTTP::Tiny Header Forwarding Flaw Exposes Credentials
item.description: The HTTP::Tiny library incorrectly forwards caller-supplied credential headers, such as Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization, during cross-origin redirects, including HTTPS to HTTP transitions. This flaw could allow attackers to capture sensitive authentication information when following redirects, potentially compromising downstream services. Users should upgrade to the latest HTTP::Tiny release and review redirect handling to mitigate credential leakage.

item.title: GitLab Issues Patches for Multiple Vulnerabilities
item.description: GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions before 19.6.2, 19.5.9, 19.4.11, 19.3.10, 19.2.11, 19.1.11, 19.0.12, and 18.11.15 contain undisclosed vulnerabilities. The advisory lacks CVE IDs, but the flaws could enable privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution within GitLab. GitLab recommends upgrading to the patched releases; administrators should apply updates promptly to mitigate the risk.

item.title: FIFA Breach Involves Limited Personal and Business Data
item.description: The Swiss-based FIFA governing body reports that hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business information. The breach does not appear to involve financial data or large-scale credential theft, but the exact scope remains under investigation. FIFA is collaborating with authorities and law enforcement to determine the extent of the compromise and implement remedial measures.

item.title: USN-9202-1: Kerberos vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause the KDC to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-107364) It was discovered that the Kerberos KDC incorrectly handled malformed client names in PAC data during S4U2Proxy requests. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-107708) It was discovered that Kerberos incorrectly handled certain KRB-CRED messages.

item.title: CVE-2026-134070 - Improper input sanitization in the AWS Config remediation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3
item.description: We identified CVE-2026-134070, where improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value.

item.title: Italy, Switzerland Warn of AI-Powered Autonomous Cyberattacks
item.description: Italian and Swiss cybersecurity agencies issued a warning about autonomous cyberattacks driven by AI agents targeting critical infrastructure organizations. The advisory highlights the increasing capability of automated threat actors to launch coordinated attacks without human intervention. Security teams should monitor for anomalous activity, enforce strict access controls, and update AI detection systems to mitigate potential threats.

item.title: NetworkManager D-Bus Privilege Escalation Exploited
item.description: A flaw in Ubuntu's NetworkManager grants the whoopsie user unrestricted D-Bus access to root-only methods, enabling local privilege escalation. The vulnerability could allow an attacker to disrupt networking, modify logging, or alter connection configurations, potentially impacting system stability. Ubuntu has released an update that restricts whoopsie D-Bus permissions; administrators should apply the patch or disable whoopsie to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Satellite 6.19 Critical Update Released
item.description: A critical update for Red Hat Satellite 6.19 patches multiple vulnerabilities that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The update includes patches for undisclosed flaws, each with a CVSS base score via CVE links, rated Critical by Red Hat Product Security. Red Hat recommends applying the Satellite 6.19 update immediately to mitigate the risk, with no additional workarounds required.

item.title: Drupal Core Vulnerability CVE-2026-136716 Exploited in Wild
item.description: Drupal core versions before 10.6.23, 11.3.23, and 11.4.14 are affected by CVE-2026-136716, a critical access-bypass flaw that attackers exploited worldwide. The flaw bypasses authentication, allowing unauthorized access to site administration and potential data exfiltration. Drupal administrators must apply the latest patch releases immediately and review vendor guidance to mitigate the vulnerability.

item.title: Hitachi Energy RTU500 Firmware Vulnerabilities Disclosed
item.description: Hitachi Energy disclosed vulnerabilities in RTU500 CMU firmware versions up to 13.9.1, 12.7.8, 13.5.4, 13.6.3, 13.7.8, and 13.8.2 via the Cosminexus component. The flaws may allow attackers to gain unauthorized control or disrupt industrial control system operations, posing safety risks. Hitachi urges users to apply the latest firmware patches promptly and review vendor documentation for update instructions.

item.title: Thanksgiving Thanks and Critiques from David
item.description: On November 25, 2026, David posted a Thanksgiving-themed note thanking the cybersecurity community and addressing threat actors. The brief message acknowledges community efforts, offers gratitude, and delivers a few pointed remarks toward malicious actors. No technical vulnerabilities or incidents are reported, making it a general commentary on community resilience today.

item.title: Socket Calm Theme Launches for VS Code, Vim, Neovim
item.description: Socket Calm, a free open-source syntax highlighting theme, has been released for VS Code, Vim, and Neovim. The theme draws inspiration from Socket's design system, offering consistent color palettes and readability enhancements across editors. Users can install the theme via the respective extension repositories or package managers, with no licensing restrictions.

item.title: Ubuntu Discloses elfutils Readelf and Strip CVEs
item.description: Ubuntu reported two elfutils CVEs that affect readelf and strip when handling malformed DWARF data or empty sections. The flaws (CVE-2025-1352 and CVE-2025-1376) could crash the utilities or enable arbitrary code execution if an attacker tricks a user or automated system into processing crafted files. Ubuntu has issued patches; updating elfutils to the latest release will mitigate the vulnerabilities.

item.title: Ghostscript Vulnerability Updated on RHEL 9
item.description: Ghostscript on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 is affected by a security flaw. The vulnerability, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, has a CVSS base score detailed in the CVE references; it permits potential exploitation of the Ghostscript interpreter. Red Hat has released an update; administrators should apply the Ghostscript patch immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Ghostscript Vulnerability Updated on RHEL 8
item.description: Ghostscript on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 is affected by a security flaw. The vulnerability, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, has a CVSS base score detailed in the CVE references; it permits potential exploitation of the Ghostscript interpreter. Red Hat has released an update; administrators should apply the Ghostscript patch immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse
item.description: The AI-powered penetration testing framework ARTEX has been abused by threat actors like Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon, and Salt Typhoon to accelerate their existing workflows related to network reconnaissance, credential attacks, and web application exploitation.

item.title: USN-9199-1: authd vulnerability
item.description: Adrian Dombeck discovered that authd incorrectly assigned user and group identifiers during first-time SSH logins. A remote authenticated user could possibly use this issue to access or modify files belonging to another user, potentially leading to account takeover or privilege escalation.

item.title: Florida Ransomware Recovery CEO Indicted
item.description: A federal grand jury indicted the CEO of a Florida-based ransomware recovery firm for allegedly lying about services and paying ransoms to cybercriminals. The indictment alleges the executive engaged in deceptive practices and facilitated financial transactions that supported ransomware operators. The case underscores the legal risks for recovery providers and signals increased scrutiny of the industry by law enforcement.

item.title: CVE-2026-136267 - Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command in Kiro Web
item.description: We are aware of CVE-2026-136267, an issue in Kiro Web where tool-call markup inside content an agent session read, such as a repository file or a web page, could be repeated by certain models and run as a command in the subscriber's hosted development environment without a consent prompt.
